description: What the deployed page actually does when it loads. Source cannot answer any of it: these fail on a build that compiled, a deploy that succeeded and a page that looks right.

gates.title: The Deployed Page Answers
gates.rule: The production URL returns the site over HTTPS, and the non-canonical host redirects to the canonical one rather than serving a second copy.
gates.fix: Fix the deployment or the DNS, and set the redirect so one host is canonical.

gates.title: The Console Is Clean
gates.rule: Loading the page produces no console errors. An error on load is a code path that already failed, and the visitor sees whatever the page was going to render after it.
gates.fix: Fix each one. An error from a third party is still an error the visitor's browser reports.

gates.title: Nothing The Page Asks For Is Missing
gates.rule: No request the page makes returns 404. A missing font, image or chunk is invisible in a build log and obvious on the page.
gates.fix: Correct the paths, or ship the files the build left out.

gates.title: Every Third Party It Loads Answers
gates.rule: Each external script or stylesheet the page pulls returns 200. A third party that stopped serving takes a piece of the page with it, and does it long after anybody was looking.
gates.fix: Remove what is gone, or self-host it. Anything about how much it weighs goes to /perf-checklist.
